key_insight: HERMES combines H&E and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) images with step-level supervision to improve tumor immune microenvironment readouts and make intermediate quantities checkable.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support pathology research by linking tissue architecture with immune-cell phenotypes, but clinical utility remains unproven.
method: Reasons jointly over paired, same-section H&E and mIF images.
Uses mIF-derived cell-level measurements to supervise guideline-based reasoning steps.
Applies reinforcement learning rewards that check stated intermediate quantities, not just final answers.
evidence_signal: Across four colorectal cancer tasks, HERMES achieved 84.5% average accuracy versus 74.7% for the strongest comparator, and retained an accuracy lead without retraining on external CODEX and head-and-neck cancer evaluations.
watch_item: Deployment would require reliable paired-image alignment and phenotype measurements, plus validation beyond the reported field-level research tasks.
paper_title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
